000
FXUS65 KPSR 022103
AFDPSR

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Phoenix AZ
203 PM MST Mon Nov 2 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Dry conditions with mostly sunny skies can be expected today,
  but flooding of area creeks, streams, and rivers will continue
  through least tonight, following runoff from significant 
  rainfall over the past few days.

- Flooding in some of the major waterways like the Salt River may 
  persist through the week.
 
- Dry and seasonal weather conditions are expected over the next
  several days, with lower desert highs gradually rising from the
  mid 70s to upper 70s by the end of this week. 

&&

.SHORT TERM /TODAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY/... 

Latest 3-day gauge measured rainfall and radar estimates show a 
large area east and northeast of Phoenix, in the foothills and 
higher terrain, received 5-7 inches and a few spots reached 8 
inches. Even though the rain has ended, there is still a significant 
amount of runoff moving through the water systems across central AZ. 
Several USGS and flood control streamflow gauges are still above 
designated action/alarm stages and some are currently in minor to 
moderate flood stage. Many areal and river flood warnings will 
remain in effect through the rest of today. Unlike winter and spring 
snowmelt runoff following a rain event, should subside more quickly. 
However, some of the major waterways and watersheds, like the Salt 
and Verde systems, will take longer to subside. Possibly through 
even most of the week. Salt River Project will continue releasing a 
very high volume (over 60000 cfs) of water from Bartlett Dam into 
the Verde River, and from Granite Reef Dam into the Salt River. 
Impacts on the Salt River downstream of Tempe Town Lake can be 
expected as high flows continue. Recreating in the Verde and Salt 
rivers will be very dangerous and is strongly discouraged. There 
have been multiple fatalities from recreation with similar flows in 
the past. Continue to heed all road closures as will and do not 
attempt to cross flooded roads.
 
Latest mid-lvl wv imagery and 500 mb streamline analysis reveals 
the trough of low pressure that passed through our region 
yesterday is now entering the Midwestern U.S. while a shortwave 
ridge builds in behind this feature over the West Coast. Winds 
will be somewhat breezy this afternoon on the backside of the 
departing trough, mainly along the lower Colorado River Valley 
where gusts could reach 20-25 mph at times. However much of the 
region will experience light winds and clear skies through the 
rest of this afternoon with highs reaching the mid 60s to low 70s 
across the lower deserts. Winds will greatly diminish tonight 
after sunset, becoming very light and calm across the area. With 
clear skies and light winds along with residual sfc moisture left 
over from yesterday's rain event, there is a chance that patchy 
fog could develop in low lying elevations early Tuesday morning. 
The most likely location for fog development will be N Pinal 
County and the Imperial Valley. 

The aforementioned shortwave ridge will pass over the forecast 
area tomorrow between the departing upper level trough and another
Pacific low. Model guidance keeps this next Pacific low on a 
west- east trajectory through UT and CO on Wednesday. Just about 
all this transient low will do to the local area is suppress 
heights and keep temperatures from warming more quickly. High 
temperatures Tuesday and Wednesday will rise by a few degrees 
area-wide, but still remain around 5 degrees below normal, with 
lower desert communities reaching the middle low to mid 70s. 
Morning temperatures the next few days will be seasonally cool, 
mostly in the 50s across the lower deserts and 40s in higher 
elevation communities and some of the typically cooler lower 
desert valley spots.

&&

.LONG TERM /THURSDAY THROUGH SUNDAY/... 

The long term forecast remains dry and seasonal. There is now
much better confidence in the late week and weekend forecast,
which favors ridging building in across the West and a weak cutoff
low forming over the Pacific west of Baja California. Weak
troughing looks to drag across the local area Friday into Saturday
ahead of the building ridge. Previous forecasts supported slight 
rain chances with this trough, but this trough now looks
completely dry and latest NBM PoPs are 5% or less across the
region. These are also the only PoPs in the 7-day forecast. Plenty
of time to dry out fallowing all the rain. Temperatures during 
the second half of the week will remain steady near to slightly 
below normal and then heading into the weekend temperatures are 
likely to trend warmer as the ridging builds into the west. Most 
lower deserts may see high temperatures return to the low and 
possibly even mid 80s.

&&

.AVIATION...Updated at 1720Z.

South Central Arizona including KPHX, KIWA, KSDL, and KDVT; 
No aviation weather issues are expected throughout the TAF 
period. The overall wind pattern will follow the more typical 
diurnal tendencies with westerly winds persisting through early 
this evening before shifting out of the east during the late 
evening hours with speeds generally aob 6 kts. Extended periods 
of light and variable to even calm conditions can be expected. FEW
cumulus clouds with decks aoa 6 kft can be expected this 
afternoon with some high cirrus cloud decks moving in during the 
overnight period. 

Southeast California/Southwest Arizona including KIPL and KBLH:
No aviation weather issues are expected throughout the TAF 
period. Winds will generally prevail out of the west to northwest 
at KIPL and out of the north at KBLH with speeds aob 10 kts, 
although some occasional gusts in the mid to upper teens will be 
possible at KBLH this afternoon. Clear skies will prevail through 
this afternoon before some high cirrus cloud decks move in by 
early this evening. 

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Lingering floodwater runoff in area creeks, streams, and rivers 
is likely to continue through tonight. Otherwise, rain has ended 
and dry seasonal conditions can be expected through the next 7 
days. Saturated grounds will help keep surface humidity levels 
somewhat elevated. Afternoon minimum RHs today will be around 
50-60% across AZ and 25-35% across southeast CA. Despite gradual 
drying through the week, the minimum RHs will only fall to around 
35-45% across AZ and 20-30% across southeast CA. Overnight 
recoveries will remain good through the week, with around 60-80% 
max RHs most nights. Winds through the next 7 days will mostly 
follow typical diurnal trends with light speeds and modest 
afternoon upslope gusts. Some breezier north winds may develop 
along the lower Colorado River Valley at times, but with only 
minor gusts up to 20-25 mph forecast at this time.

&&

.PSR WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
AZ...None.
CA...None.
&&

$$

SHORT TERM...Salerno/Benedict
LONG TERM...Benedict
AVIATION...Lojero
FIRE WEATHER...Benedict
